parts.title: Sermo sancti Bernárdi Abbátis
parts.source: Serm. in cap. 12 Apoc., ante med.
paragraphs: Amplectámur Maríæ vestígia, fratres mei, et devotíssima supplicatióne beátis illíus pédibus provolvámur. Teneámus eam nec dimittámus, donec benedíxerit nobis; potens est enim. Nempe vellus est médium inter rorem et áream: múlier inter solem et lunam: María inter Christum et Ecclésiam constitúta. Sed forte miráris, non tam vellus opértum rore, quam amíctam sole mulíerem. Magna síquidem familiáritas, sed mira omníno vicínitas solis et mulíeris. Quómodo enim in tam veheménti fervóre tam frágilis natúra subsístit? Mérito quidem admiráris, Móyses sancte, et curiósius desíderas intuéri. Verúmtamen solve calceaménta de pédibus tuis, et involúcra pone carnálium cogitatiónum, si accédere concupíscis.

responsory.text: Felix namque es, sacra Virgo María, et omni laude digníssima:
responsory.repeat: Quia ex te ortus est sol justítiæ, Christus, Deus noster.

responsory.text: Ora pro pópulo, intérveni pro clero, intercéde pro devóto femíneo sexu: séntiant omnes tuum juvámen, quicúmque célebrant tuam sanctam commemoratiónem.
Quia ex te ortus est sol justítiæ.
Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

parts.title: A sermon of St. Bernard, Abbot
parts.source: Sermon of ch. 12 of the Apocalypse, in the first half
paragraphs: My brothers, let us cast ourselves at Mary's blessed feet with the most devout supplication. Let us embrace them, let us hold fast to her, and not let go until she blesses us; for she has great power. Like the fleece between the dew and the threshing floor, like the woman between the sun and the moon, so Mary stands between Christ and the Church. But perhaps you wonder, not so much at the fleece covered with dew, but at the woman clothed with the sun. Any relationship between the sun and the woman would be striking enough, but this proximity is indeed something to be marveled at. How can so fragile a nature subsist in that excessive heat? You have a right to wonder, saintly Moses; it is only natural that in your curiosity you should want to look more closely. But “remove the sandals from your feet”, put aside the covering of fleshly thoughts, if you wish to draw near.

responsory.text: O Holy Virgin Mary, happy indeed art thou, and right worthy of all praise
responsory.repeat: For out of thee rose the Sun of righteousness, even Christ our God.

responsory.text: Pray for the people, plead for the clergy, make intercession for all women vowed to God. Let all that are making this holy memorial of thee feel the might of thine assistance.
For out of thee rose the Sun of righteousness.
Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

Matins · Saturday, 17 October 2026

Our Lady’s Saturday

Sanctæ Mariæ Sabbato · Simplex

Read in Latin and English

Short lesson

A sermon of St. Bernard, Abbot

Sermon of ch. 12 of the Apocalypse, in the first half

My brothers, let us cast ourselves at Mary's blessed feet with the most devout supplication. Let us embrace them, let us hold fast to her, and not let go until she blesses us; for she has great power. Like the fleece between the dew and the threshing floor, like the woman between the sun and the moon, so Mary stands between Christ and the Church. But perhaps you wonder, not so much at the fleece covered with dew, but at the woman clothed with the sun. Any relationship between the sun and the woman would be striking enough, but this proximity is indeed something to be marveled at. How can so fragile a nature subsist in that excessive heat? You have a right to wonder, saintly Moses; it is only natural that in your curiosity you should want to look more closely. But “remove the sandals from your feet”, put aside the covering of fleshly thoughts, if you wish to draw near.

℟. O Holy Virgin Mary, happy indeed art thou, and right worthy of all praise * For out of thee rose the Sun of righteousness, even Christ our God.

℣. Pray for the people, plead for the clergy, make intercession for all women vowed to God. Let all that are making this holy memorial of thee feel the might of thine assistance.

℟. For out of thee rose the Sun of righteousness.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Even Christ our God.

Serm. in cap. 12 Apoc., ante med.

Sermon of ch. 12 of the Apocalypse, in the first half

Amplectámur Maríæ vestígia, fratres mei, et devotíssima supplicatióne beátis illíus pédibus provolvámur. Teneámus eam nec dimittámus, donec benedíxerit nobis; potens est enim. My brothers, let us cast ourselves at Mary's blessed feet with the most devout supplication. Let us embrace them, let us hold fast to her, and not let go until she blesses us; for she has great power. Like the fleece between the dew and the threshing floor, like the woman between the sun and the moon, so Mary stands between Christ and the Church. But perhaps you wonder, not so much at the fleece covered with dew, but at the woman clothed with the sun. Any relationship between the sun and the woman would be striking enough, but this proximity is indeed something to be marveled at. How can so fragile a nature subsist in that excessive heat? You have a right to wonder, saintly Moses; it is only natural that in your curiosity you should want to look more closely. But “remove the sandals from your feet”, put aside the covering of fleshly thoughts, if you wish to draw near.

℟. Felix namque es, sacra Virgo María, et omni laude digníssima: * Quia ex te ortus est sol justítiæ, Christus, Deus noster.

℟. O Holy Virgin Mary, happy indeed art thou, and right worthy of all praise * For out of thee rose the Sun of righteousness, even Christ our God.

℣. Ora pro pópulo, intérveni pro clero, intercéde pro devóto femíneo sexu: séntiant omnes tuum juvámen, quicúmque célebrant tuam sanctam commemoratiónem.

℣. Pray for the people, plead for the clergy, make intercession for all women vowed to God. Let all that are making this holy memorial of thee feel the might of thine assistance.

℟. Quia ex te ortus est sol justítiæ.

℟. For out of thee rose the Sun of righteousness.

℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.

℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

℟. Christus, Deus noster.

℟. Even Christ our God.
